purpose: Pravastatin is used to lower high cholesterol and triglycerides (fats) in your blood. It helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and other heart-related problems. Doctors also prescribe it to protect your heart if you already have heart disease or are at high risk.
how_it_works: Your liver naturally makes cholesterol, and pravastatin works by blocking a key enzyme the liver uses to produce it. This brings down the level of 'bad' cholesterol (LDL) in your blood and can raise your 'good' cholesterol (HDL). Think of it as turning down the dial on your liver's cholesterol-making machine.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate pravastatin well. Some may notice mild muscle aches or soreness, headache, nausea, stomach upset, or diarrhea. These effects are usually mild and often go away as your body adjusts.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine — this could be a rare but serious muscle problem. Pravastatin can affect your liver, so avoid drinking excessive alcohol. Do not take it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm a baby. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medications you take, since some drugs can interact with pravastatin.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 40 mg once a day, taken at any time of day with or without food. Your doctor may adjust your dose (typically between 10 mg and 80 mg daily) based on your cholesterol levels and how well you respond to the medication. Try to take it at the same time each day to build a routine.
